items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: So I messed around Newark, New Jersey until I kept studying with a man named Emory Lucas, music.

ctx.x: I was about 17 then. Newark, New Jersey, there weren't many people of color there. Most of them Indian people, mixed Indian people and German people. And naturally they had the white man and that's what was happening. And so I got stranded and then I went home. Then I went back with the Bluebirds and I stayed and saved myself up about a couple hundred dollars and got a couple of nice suits and then I said, but I'm going, so I come right back to Newark, New Jersey, but I had met a little girl up there and I went…
So I messed around Newark, New Jersey until I kept studying with a man named Emory Lucas, music.

he says, well, Jack, why don't you go up to the Big Apple and see a man named Professor Jackson, so I says okay, and I went up there and Professor Jackson, couldn't hardly hold the clarinet and so they had another fellow named Joe Crump and Joe Crump had a whole set of gold teeth and had diamonds on each side and this little funny looking place, so he says well, can you play anything so I played the melody and he said, that's nice, so he said can you come to work, and so Jackson said yes, so then come to work…
